bugs.error_message: validate-mermaid.sh: Chromium path macOS-only; scratch file cleanup swallows diagnostics on failure
bugs.root_cause: Script only searched ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright (macOS). On Linux the path is ~/.cache/ms-playwright. Also, rm -f $SCRATCH ran unconditionally before the exit code check, destroying diagnostic output on failure.
bugs.fix: Added Linux fallback path. Added npx playwright install chromium auto-install if both paths empty. Moved rm -f $SCRATCH to after diagnostic output is printed on failure; rm immediately on success.

bugs.error_message: 429 Client Error: Too Many Requests for url: https://api-web.nhle.com/v1/roster/ANA/current
bugs.root_cause: 32 sequential roster API calls with no delay saturate the NHL API rate limit after ~20 requests. No retry logic in _get() helper.
bugs.fix: Added time.sleep(0.5) between roster calls in load_rosters.py. Added exponential backoff retry (3/6/12/24s) in api_client._get() on 429 status codes.

bugs.root_cause: Players on IR or non-roster assignments appear in boxscore playerByGameStats but are absent from /v1/roster/{team}/current. FK on player_id references players table which only contains current roster.
bugs.fix: Added _ensure_player() helper that checks players table first, then stub-inserts from boxscore name.default + playerId if missing. Called before every player_game_stats insert.

bugs.error_message: No subschema in "anyOf" matched... "required_pull_request_reviews", "required_status_checks" weren't supplied. For allOf/0, "true" is not a boolean.
bugs.root_cause: gh api nested-field shorthand (-f required_status_checks.strict=true) sends booleans and nested objects as literal strings, not JSON types, so GitHub's schema validation for PUT .../branches/main/protection rejects the request with HTTP 422.
bugs.fix: Switched to a raw JSON body via --input - with a heredoc instead of -f flags for this endpoint.

bugs.error_message: Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature. (HTTP 403)
bugs.root_cause: Classic branch protection rules on a private repo require a paid GitHub plan (Pro/Team/Enterprise) on personal accounts; free-tier private repos are rejected outright.
bugs.fix: Confirmed with user, scanned tracked files for secrets, then made the repo public via gh repo edit --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences before retrying branch protection.

bugs.error_message: gitleaks: Failed to load config error="[[allowlists]] must contain at least one check for: commits, paths, regexes, or stopwords"
bugs.root_cause: gitleaks requires TOML array-of-tables syntax `[[allowlists]]` with at least one check field (commits/paths/regexes/stopwords); a placeholder `[allowlist]` table with only a `description` key and no check field is rejected outright rather than treated as a no-op.
bugs.fix: Removed the empty allowlist table entirely and left a comment explaining that a real `[[allowlists]]` block should only be added once there's a proven false positive to scope it to — an intentionally absent section, not an empty placeholder.

bugs.error_message: npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills --skill=grill-me,grilling,codebase-design,domain-modeling,teach --global -y installed all 36 skills to every detected agent (Claude Code, Cline, GitHub Copilot, etc.) instead of the 5 named
bugs.root_cause: The `-s/--skill` flag on the `skills` CLI does not reliably filter the target skill set in non-interactive mode (auto-detected agent, no TTY) — it falls back to installing everything found in the source repo, regardless of a comma-separated --skill value.
bugs.fix: Let the over-broad install complete, then used `npx skills remove <name1> <name2> ... --global -y` (space-separated positional args, confirmed reliable) to prune down to exactly the intended skill set. Verified the final state with `ls ~/.claude/skills/` and `git status` rather than trusting the CLI's own success output.

bugs.error_message: fatal: not a valid object name: '68b6303'
bugs.root_cause: Two Bash tool calls sent in the same message run in parallel, each in its own subshell — a `cd` in one does not carry over to the other. `cd langsmith-plugin && git branch -f local-customizations e240c52` ran in call 1; a bare `git branch -f local-customizations 68b6303` (no cd) ran in call 2, executing from the original ~/.claude cwd instead of superpowers/, so the target sha couldn't be resolved.
bugs.fix: Re-ran the second command with an explicit `cd /Users/paulmckay/.claude/superpowers && git branch -f local-customizations 68b6303` instead of relying on directory state from a sibling parallel call.

bugs.error_message: ~1,076 players permanently skipped by enrich_players.py — bio fields (height/weight/birth_date/birth_country) never populated
bugs.root_cause: WHERE clause combined `is_active IS NULL OR (is_active=1 AND ...)` — players with is_active=0 and enriched_at=NULL (set by a run before the enriched_at column existed) matched neither branch and were permanently skipped
bugs.fix: Changed to `WHERE enriched_at IS NULL OR (is_active=1 AND enriched_at < datetime('now','-7 days'))` — orthogonal conditions, each independently catches its case regardless of is_active value

bugs.error_message: Players loaded via upsert_player_stub() have null height/weight/birth_date/birth_country even after enrichment runs
bugs.root_cause: upsert_player_enrichment() UPDATE statement did not include height_inches, weight_pounds, birth_date, birth_country — fields present in landing API response (heightInInches, weightInPounds, birthDate, birthCountry) were never written
bugs.fix: Added COALESCE(height_inches, ?), COALESCE(weight_pounds, ?), COALESCE(birth_date, ?), COALESCE(birth_country, ?) to UPDATE SET; added corresponding values to parameter tuple and extraction in enrich_players.py

bugs.error_message: pull-skills.mjs sync script silently dropped 8 of 27 skills (brainstorming, receiving-code-review, requesting-code-review, systematic-debugging, test-driven-development, using-git-worktrees, verification-before-completion, writing-plans)
bugs.root_cause: syncSkills() and findNestedMarkdownFiles() filtered directory entries with Dirent.isDirectory(), which reflects the entry's own type and returns false for symlinks — it does not follow the link. Skills sourced from the superpowers submodule are installed into skills/ as symlinks (e.g. skills/brainstorming -> /Users/paulmckay/.claude/superpowers/skills/brainstorming), so they were silently excluded from readdirSync filtering with no warning.
bugs.fix: Replaced Dirent.isDirectory()/isFile() checks with statSync(fullPath).isDirectory()/.isFile(), which follows symlinks to the real target.
